assumptions.text: Scratchpads remain plain Markdown files on disk under ~/.insrc/scratches/ so they stay editable outside VS Code and diffable in git when inside a workspace; all linking/indexing is metadata layered on that contract, not a new file format.

VS Code's bundled markdown-language-features custom editor (vscode.markdown.editor) provides rendered-in-place editing with lock/inline-edit on standard VS Code installs (user-verified, 2026-11-15), so the pad surface should not need a bespoke rich-text webview — but availability across every host this plugin targets is unverified: vscode-plugin/src/hosts/specs.ts already treats Cursor as a distinct host, and the plugin elsewhere anticipates a capability missing in an editor fork (chat/group-lock.ts). S1 must detect the capability per host rather than assume it everywhere.

The daemon's existing graph + doc-relations layer can resolve link targets to files, symbols, and workflow artifacts by extending the file-target-only link extraction, without widening repo enrollment to the home-dir scratchpad store.

The user's PRD mock decisions are settled inputs (10-pad recent menu, 20-pad/3-line list panel with in-panel relevance search, per-row delete, native editor with lock/pencil, separate find-in-note), not open questions for design.

constraints.text: Two distinct search surfaces: cross-note relevance search lives only in the list panel; find-in-note (Ctrl/Cmd+F) stays a separate in-pad action operating on live unsaved text, independent of lock state.

UI parameters are fixed by the PRD mock: recent menu cap 10; list panel cap 20 newest-first with first-3-line previews and per-row delete; relevance ranking puts title hits ahead of body-only hits, ties by mtime then stable id.

The pad uses Milkdown + Crepe in one VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider pane backed by its real .md TextDocument. Insrc owns rendered editing, lock/pencil controls and a selection Send action; selecting text alone sends nothing, and clicking Send inserts selected text into the chat composer without submission. VS Code owns the document save/conflict/backup lifecycle; synchronization and undo integration must be verified. Replace the legacy textarea and document-save protocol; the host built-in Markdown editor is no longer required.

The home-dir scratchpad store stays outside repo enrollment and default document search; daemon-backed backlinks join only through a private, repository-keyed scratchpad index using validated target identity (note=repo+stable ID; file/symbol=repo+path+qualified name; artifact=repo+canonical ID).
No implicit agent context: note evidence enters a turn or workflow draft only on explicit user selection (SP-5/SP-6), never by default.

Non-goals are binding: no vault import/sync, shared/collaborative editing, general-purpose canvas/graph browser, unlinked-mention suggestions, arbitrary transclusion, automatic project-memory ingestion, CLI/JetBrains surfaces, semantic embedding search, or analyzer-output links in this epic.

body.problem: A scratchpad today is a flat, unlinked Markdown file: easy to find when recent (the chat menu shows five), impossible to rediscover from the code, symbol, or workflow artifact it concerns, and read-only-ish once opened in the plugin's custom webview. There is no way to link notes to each other or to tracked design/code, no backlinks from a file or artifact back to the notes that discuss it, no cross-note search (only an unbounded browse list), no dated entries or stable identity across rename/archive, and no way to carry a note selection into a chat turn or promote it into a tracked workflow draft. The scratchpad corpus therefore stays a pile of recent files rather than a second knowledge surface sitting beside the indexed code graph and the workflow ledger.

summary.prose: Turns the VS Code scratchpads from a flat list of recent files into a linked knowledge surface: pads open in one Milkdown + Crepe editor pane backed by the real Markdown file and VS Code TextDocument, notes link to each other and to code symbols and workflow artifacts with visible backlinks, the list panel and in-pad find make the corpus searchable, and dated entries, stable IDs, and archive/delete lifecycle make notes durable. Note evidence can be explicitly attached to a chat turn or promoted into a tracked SPEC/ISSUE draft — never implicitly.

body.title: Linked scratchpads in VS Code

requirements.statement: A scratchpad can contain typed links to other scratchpads, workspace files, code symbols, and workflow artifacts (SPEC/ISSUE/HLD/LLD/TASK), with qualified targets that resolve unambiguously and distinguishable ambiguous/missing/unavailable states; links inside code spans/blocks stay literal.
requirements.rationale: The PRD's P0 slice; links/backlinks only pay off alongside search and lifecycle.

requirements.statement: The system shows outgoing and incoming links for a note, and surfaces scratchpad backlinks on file and symbol views, grouped by source note; backlinks on a workflow artifact's own detail view follow once vscode-plugin has a persistent per-artifact surface to host them (none exists today).
requirements.rationale: Rediscovery of notes from the code or design they concern; the artifact-surface slice is deferred pending that surface (see open questions).

requirements.statement: The "insrc scratchpads" list panel shows up to 20 pads newest-first with first-3-line previews and per-row delete, and a search box that filters the list by relevance (title hits first, then mtime, then stable id); any card opens the pad. The chat recent menu shows up to 10 pads by mtime alongside New/Browse-all.
requirements.rationale: Settled UI: search box in the list panel, not a nav view and not inside the pad.

requirements.statement: An in-pad find action highlights matches with an N-of-M count and prev/next wraparound, closable with Escape, showing a zero-match state, operating on live text regardless of editor lock state.
requirements.rationale: Find inside the open pad is a separate surface per the mock.

requirements.statement: A pad opens in one Milkdown + Crepe rendered/editable editor pane on its real .md TextDocument with lock/pencil controls, rich image/link authoring and an explicit selection Send icon; normal VS Code document save/conflict/backup behavior applies through a verified synchronization bridge.
requirements.rationale: Pad editing must feel native, not like a custom webview.

requirements.statement: Notes carry dated entries in day-grouped newest-first collapsible sections with an Undated bucket for legacy content, plus a stable ID surviving rename/move/archive/restore, reversible archive, and explicit permanent delete.
requirements.rationale: P0 lifecycle portion of SP-4.

requirements.statement: A user can explicitly attach selected note excerpts to a chat turn, with a removable preview showing source and revision, bounded to the controller/daemon payload routes, pinning the revision for queued turns.
requirements.rationale: P1: evidence into a turn only on explicit selection.

requirements.statement: A user can promote a saved note selection into a workflow draft (SPEC via brainstorm or ISSUE) through the existing approval chain, with a provenance link back on the note and idempotent retry.
requirements.rationale: P1: promotion through the existing approval chain.

requirements.statement: Notes can carry optional tags (filterable in the list panel) and starter templates for investigations/decision candidates.
requirements.rationale: P2 per PRD, independent of the link machinery once metadata exists.

requirements.statement: A pad opens as a single Milkdown + Crepe rendered/editable Markdown pane on its real VS Code TextDocument, with insrc-owned pencil/lock controls; selecting text reveals a Send icon, and only clicking it inserts the bounded selection into chat without submitting.
requirements.rationale: Approved HLD revision 5 replaces the built-in-editor-only implementation while preserving the single-pane rich Markdown experience and existing explicit selected-text insertion.

requirements.statement: Image paste/drop, URL-to-link paste, and insert-link/insert-image-from-workspace work in the pad editor.
requirements.rationale: Rich authoring affordances without bespoke code.

requirements.statement: The list panel carries a search box that filters the recency list by relevance with title-first ranking and mtime/id tiebreaks, and clearing restores the full list.
requirements.rationale: SP-3 'Search all notes' as settled: the search box lives in the list panel, not a nav view and not inside the pad.

requirements.statement: The list panel caps at 20 newest-first pads with 3-line previews and per-row delete; the chat recent menu caps at 10.
requirements.rationale: Capped, previewed list with delete per settled mock.

requirements.statement: An in-pad find highlights matches with N-of-M count, wraparound prev/next, Escape to close, and a zero-match state, operating on live text regardless of lock state.
requirements.rationale: SP-3 'Find in note' — the separate in-pad surface.

requirements.statement: Pads support dated entries rendered as day-grouped, newest-first, collapsible sections with per-day counts and an Undated bucket for legacy notes.
requirements.rationale: SP-4 'Dated entries'.

requirements.statement: Pads support typed links to notes, files, symbols, and workflow artifacts, with a target picker, qualified-target commit for duplicate titles/symbols, distinguishable ambiguous/missing/unavailable states with repair, and literal links inside code spans/blocks.
requirements.rationale: SP-1 link authoring + resolution across all four target types.

requirements.statement: Outgoing and incoming links are visible on a note; file and symbol views show scratchpad backlinks grouped by source note. Backlinks on a workflow artifact's own detail view are deferred until vscode-plugin has a durable per-artifact surface to host them.
requirements.rationale: SP-2 backlinks, on note + target surfaces; deferred for workflow artifacts pending a surface.

requirements.statement: Every pad carries a stable ID surviving rename/move/archive/restore, explicit repo association for legacy notes, reversible archive (hidden from default search/backlinks, direct link still opens), and explicit permanent delete with 'missing' link rendering.
requirements.rationale: SP-4 identity/lifecycle (not dated entries).

requirements.statement: A user can explicitly attach selected note excerpts to a chat turn, with a removable preview showing source/revision, bounded payload, and revision pinning for queued turns.
requirements.rationale: SP-5 cited agent context — explicit only.

requirements.statement: A saved note selection can be promoted into a SPEC or ISSUE draft through the existing approval chain, with a provenance link back on the note and idempotent retry after a lost response.
requirements.rationale: SP-6 promote to workflow draft through the existing approval chain.

requirements.statement: Notes carry optional tags (filterable in the list panel) and starter templates are offered at pad creation.
requirements.rationale: SP-7 tags + templates.

citations.quotedText: Settled mock UI decisions: menu cap 10; list panel 20 pads newest-first, 3-line previews, per-row delete, in-panel relevance search; pad = built-in Markdown Editor locked with pencil inline-edit; separate in-pad find.
Flat ~/.insrc/scratches/*.md store, basename IDs, guarded read/write.
Custom webview document view (documentBodyHtml/documentBootstrap, scratch-save/scratch-saved); unbounded browse list (browseHtml/renderBrowse/openBrowse) with per-row open/delete icons.
Daemon link extraction targets files only, strips fragments; no symbol/artifact resolution, no backlink projection.

The plugin's own dependencies are { "marked": "^4.3.0" } only; vscode-plugin/src contains no reference to vscode.markdown.editor or markdown-language-features anywhere — the plugin implements no built-in rich-markdown editor integration today.
Story split S1-S10, dependencies, rollout order, open decisions (link syntax, entry anchors, backlink projection, IPC version negotiation).
SCRATCH_MENU_LIMIT = 5 chat dropdown with New/Browse-all actions (chat-panel.ts menu render).

Confirmed on the user's VS Code install: `code --list-extensions --show-versions` lists markdown-language-features@10.0.0; its manifest registers customEditors vscode.markdown.preview.editor and vscode.markdown.editor ('Markdown Editor') for *.md, with toggleLocked, insertLinkFromWorkspace, insertImageFromWorkspace commands and markdown.editor.filePaste.enabled / drop.enabled settings; behavior matched against an attached screenshot of its inline-edit/lock UI. This is the HOST's bundled extension, not part of this repo.

Host detection enumerates by-editor-env hosts including Cursor (appName: 'Cursor', uriScheme: 'cursor'); vscode-plugin/src/chat/group-lock.ts:89 already anticipates 'an editor fork without it [a capability]' as an expected case elsewhere in this codebase. No comparable per-host check exists yet for vscode.markdown.editor's availability.

Its own header states it 'lists the daemon's PENDING tracked artifacts' and 'is a PASSTHROUGH observer of the tracked-workflow flow... it keeps which document is open and nothing else' — an artifact drops out once no longer pending. No persistent per-artifact detail surface exists in vscode-plugin today for backlinks to attach to.

The define workflow's own finalize step bound this Epic's unit head to a real, OPEN GitHub issue (insors-ai/insrc#185, created 2026-11-16T07:56:46Z, titled and bodied from this Epic's problem/non-goals) without tracker.push ever being called, and without present/ask/approve. User decision (2026-11-16): leave #185 as-is; record the gap here rather than close or edit the issue.

env.getExtension(detection.extensionId) is an existing, reusable by-extension host-capability check (HostEnv.getExtension, vscode-plugin/src/hosts/types.ts:33; wired via vscode.extensions.getExtension(id) !== undefined in vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts:151). Checking for 'vscode.markdown-language-features' reuses this mechanism directly — it is not an open design question, only its negative-result fallback UX needs design.

contributes.menus has only commandPalette and editor/title; contributes.commands lists 20 entries with no 'scratch' or 'link' command among them. No existing context-menu/command contribution is scoped to a file or symbol — a 'show scratchpad backlinks' action on a file/symbol needs a new command + menu contribution, not reuse of an existing one.

ArtifactIds is 'the one identity scheme for every artifact' — it already builds and parses every artifact id form (DEF-<h>, LLD-<h>-s1, TASK-<h>-s1-t3, AMD-<h>-2, ...) and RequirementIds does the same for FR ids. The workflow-artifact leg of link-target identity (SPEC/ISSUE/HLD/LLD/TASK) reuses this directly; what's new is validating a parsed id against the real artifact store and rendering missing/ambiguous states, not inventing artifact identity from scratch.

createAttachmentStore already copies a reference into the session's own directory, assigns it a stable id, and enforces size/count limits (MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_MESSAGE); its attachments field flows through chat-outbox.ts, chat-queue-store.ts and chat-queue-worker.ts — the existing queued-turn pipeline. File/image-shaped, not note-excerpt-shaped, but substantial prior art for s8's attach/preview/queue mechanics.

ScratchEntry is {id, name, mtime, size} only; `name` is 'Reconstructed from the id (the <yyyymmdd-hhmmss>-<slug> basename)' — a lossy slug, not the title text typed. listScratches() is pure readdir+stat; it reads no file content. Neither a real title nor body preview text exists today for the list to show.
